text: **dsh-prompt-balance**（DSH 桌面插件）：测量系统提示词各段的字节组成，并帮助操作协议优先于规则出现。它注册提示词组装和 agent pre-step 两个钩子：前者记录各段大小并在尚未存在时把操作协议插到段落开头，后者在 agent 指令消息前加入身份提要。可配置身份内容和操作检查清单，并将运行信息写入本地日志。适合希望观察提示词构成、调整指令顺序并保留身份上下文的 DSH 用户；不需要 API 密钥。

**dsh-prompt-balance** (DSH desktop plugin) measures system prompt section sizes, logs byte counts, and prepends an operating protocol. A second hook adds an identity digest before agent instructions. Users can customize the identity and checklist; the plugin writes a local log and needs no API key.
想知道系统提示词里规则和其他内容各占多少。
让 DSH 在规则之前先放上操作流程提示。
I want to keep an identity summary in agent instructions before context compression.
**dsh-prompt-balance** 的功能「提示词统计与协议前置」：组装系统提示词时记录各段字节数，并在协议段尚不存在时把操作协议插到最前面；通过 system-prompt/assemble 钩子自动触发。

dsh-prompt-balance README · dsh-prompt-balance：Measure what your system prompt is actually made of — then make sure the model reads the
operating protocol before it reads the prohibitions.

Works on DeepSeek Harness (DSH). Two hooks, no build step, no dependencies.

---

dsh-prompt-balance README · The problem：Long-running agents accumulate rules: an `AGENTS.md` that grew to 65 KB, a workspace
policy, a template guide, a data-security annex. Nobody measures the result. In one real
case the breakdown was **65% rules / 10.7% identity** — the model's first screen of text was
fourteen kilobytes of "don't", almost nothing about who it was working for or what good work
looked like.

Two consequences follow:

dsh-prompt-balance README · The problem：1. You cannot argue about prompt quality without numbers. "My prompt feels bloated" is not
   actionable; "rules are 42,331 bytes of 64,902, and they sit first" is.
2. Order matters. Instructions near the front of the assembly carry more weight than the
   same instructions buried after a wall of constraints.

dsh-prompt-balance README · What it does：| Hook | Effect |
|---|---|
| `system-prompt/assemble` | Writes every section's byte size to `~/.dsh/prompt-balance.log`, then prepends one short `<operator-protocol>` block **before** all rule sections. Idempotent: it will not stack a second gate. |
| `agent/pre-step` | `AGENTS.md` arrives as an ordinary message, so context compression treats it as history and can summarize the specifics away. This hook prefixes a ~250-byte identity digest so the "who am I serving" frame survives the fold. |

dsh-prompt-balance README · Install：```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-prompt-balance

dsh-prompt-balance README · or, to try a local checkout first:：dsh plugin --profile desktop add link:/absolute/path/to/dsh-prompt-balance
```

Restart the app. The plugin logs one line at install and one line per assembly, so you can
verify it is live:
bash
tail -f ~/.dsh/prompt-balance.log
```

names a real person doing real work. Create `~/.dsh/prompt-balance.json`:

{
  "identity": [
    "I am the assistant to one person: a regional manager running a multi-city store network",
    "Their output is analysis, slide decks, and operating ledgers.",

Both keys are optional and independent:
section: Configure — this is the part that matters

text:
dsh-prompt-balance README · Configure — this is the part that matters：- `identity` — a string array, joined with newlines. Used in the gate **and** in the pre-step digest.
- `gate` — a string array. First line is the framing sentence, the rest are the numbered checks.

Delete the file to return to defaults. Nothing else in the plugin is configurable, and it
never writes to your config.

dsh-prompt-balance README · What you get in the log：`in`/`out`/`gate` are byte counts, so you can prove the cost of the gate itself. `rules` is
the sum of sections whose names match `instruction|agents|workspace|memory|rule`; if your
host names its sections differently, that number is meaningless — read the `top=` list instead.

dsh-prompt-balance README · Compatibility：- DSH kernel `0.2.1-rc.*` and later. Verified against `@deepseek-ai/dsh-system-prompt`
  `lib/index.js:398` — the waterfall passes `(assembly, context, next)`, three parameters.
  A handler declared with four parameters throws `next is not a function` and takes every
  tool call down with it; this plugin declares three.
- Node 20+. No runtime dependencies.
- Nothing throws at import time: a failed loader entry makes the desktop app show its
  recovery dialog, so every step is wrapped and reported to the log instead.

dsh-prompt-balance README · Uninstall：```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop remove dsh-prompt-balance
```

The log file stays at `~/.dsh/prompt-balance.log`; delete it yourself if you want it gone.
